topic.title: Graphs — BFS & DFS traversal patterns
topic.concept: Graphs are adjacency lists or matrices; BFS finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs, DFS answers connectivity and cycle questions. Most grid problems are graphs in disguise.
points: Both traversals are O(V+E) with an adjacency list; the matrix costs O(V^2).
BFS layer-by-layer with a queue gives shortest unweighted paths; track visited BEFORE enqueue to avoid duplicates.
Cycle detection: DFS with three colors (white/gray/black) for directed; union-find for undirected.
Topological sort = DFS post-order reversed, or Kahn's algorithm with in-degrees (detects cycles when output < V).
Bar problems: Number of Islands, Clone Graph, Course Schedule, Rotting Oranges (multi-source BFS).
topic.angle: 'Why BFS here and not DFS?' — interviewers probe whether you map problem constraints (shortest path? all paths? cycle?) to the traversal, not whether you memorized the code.
